message.content:
Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe. Its key properties include:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **Standard state** | Gas at room temperature |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (13.99 K) |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g/L at STP |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L/mol at STP |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV |
| **Bond dissociation energy** | 436 kJ/mol (H₂) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and other elements |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular H₂) |
| **Physical appearance** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, HF, etc. |
| **Uses** | Fuel (fuel cells, rockets), industrial feedstock (ammonia, methanol), laboratory reagent, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents), etc. |

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements and central to many fields—from chemistry and physics to energy technology and biology.
